title: Review schematic appearance and connectivity separately
summary: Review organization, connections and annotations, then inspect a rendered sheet and verify electrical connectivity.
applies_to: Schematic visual review; editorial convention informed by the cited background.
verification: Check the exported view as well as ERC.
limitations: Editorial convention, not a source-mandated rule. This checklist is not an automatic layout or correctness guarantee.

citations.locator: Tips On How to Create Readable Schematics; Use the Power of Your CAD Tools

title: Keep a consistent signal-flow convention
summary: Prefer inputs left and outputs right so the main path is easy to follow.
applies_to: Schematic visual review; retain cited tool or library scope.
verification: Trace the main path without searching across the sheet.
limitations: Feedback, bidirectional links and bridges need exceptions; do not change circuitry for appearance.

title: Group related circuitry with meaningful headings
summary: Keep each functional circuit together and identify its purpose with a short heading.
applies_to: Schematic visual review; retain cited tool or library scope.
verification: Check that group boundaries are understandable.
limitations: A small sheet can contain several groups; one sheet per block is not mandatory.

title: Use hierarchy to make large designs navigable
summary: Use meaningful sheet names and a top-level view of subsystem connections.
applies_to: Schematic visual review; retain cited tool or library scope.
verification: Follow an interface from overview to detail.
limitations: Excessive nesting can hinder review; select depth for the design.

title: Draw repeated channels consistently
summary: Editorial convention: align equivalent channels and keep their component ordering consistent; clearly identify channel differences.
applies_to: Schematic visual review; editorial convention informed by the cited background.
limitations: Editorial convention, not a source-mandated rule. Do not copy incorrect values or join independent nets to create symmetry.

title: Reserve space for annotations and wire escape
summary: Editorial convention: reserve room around pin groups for wires, labels and nearby supporting components before filling the page.
applies_to: Schematic visual review; editorial convention informed by the cited background.
verification: Check crowded regions at output scale.
limitations: Editorial convention, not a source-mandated rule. There is no universal millimeter gap; enlarge or split the drawing rather than shrink everything.

citations.locator: PCB Symbols for Integrated Circuits; The Left-Hand Side

title: Use a connectivity-compatible schematic grid
summary: For KiCad 9 standard symbols, use the recommended 50 mil (1.27 mm) connection grid.
applies_to: Schematic visual review; retain cited tool or library scope.
limitations: A PCB placement grid is not a schematic connection grid.

title: Arrange symbol pins for function, not package shape
summary: Group related pins logically while preserving their physical pin-number mapping.
applies_to: Schematic visual review; retain cited tool or library scope.
verification: Verify each pin number after symbol changes.
limitations: KLC is a library convention, not authorization to swap electrical pins.
